title: Juan Sebastián Uribe-Quintero
text:
Juan Sebastián Uribe-Quintero
PhD Candidate in Public Administration


  
    
  


  I am a PhD Candidate at Syracuse University's Maxwell School of Citizenship and Public Affairs and a Fulbright Fellow from Colombia.
  My research focuses on understanding how political and institutional factors shape the content of policies in the policy formulation process. I study different dynamics of the policy process, such as how the policy process is shaped by executive and legislative politics, how policies assign authorities and responsibilities to different types of policymaking actors, and how key aspects of policy design (e.g., complexity and discretion) evolve through the policymaking process.
  In my dissertation, I analyze how policy content, complexity, and the delegation of authority change across each stage of the legislative process in Colombia, focusing on approved environmental policies. For this, I use a combination of quantitative and qualitative tools.
  I complement my scholarly approach with my legal training as a lawyer and my professional experience working in the Congress of Colombia as an advisor to a legislator, which allows me to approach policymaking with a practitioner's consideration of policy design choices.
  I am on the job market 2026-2027. Find my most updated CV here.

title: Research
text:
Research Interests and Agenda

My research agenda focuses on the art and craft of policy content. I want to understand how legislators and political actors’ discussions shape the language of policies, how said language changes, and how power, discretion, and responsibilities are allocated through it.
I use a mix of text-as-data methods (including the Institutional Grammar), comparative case analysis, and formal theory to trace these dynamics across the legislative process.
